title: Ayurveda Exposed: Science of Life or Signs of Death?
description:
Ayurveda is often called the Science of Life (Ayur-Veda). But is it really science, or just superstition dressed up as wisdom? In this episode of Pale Blue Thoughts, we dive into the bizarre world of Caraka Samhita and its so-called “signs of death.”

According to these texts, if your teeth are too white, you’re about to die. If your eyes are slanted, constantly open, closed, blinking, or the wrong color — death is near. If your hair comes out without pain, bad news. If your joints don’t crack when you try, you’re beyond repair. And it gets worse: dreaming of drinking urine with ghosts, seeing the sun at night or the moon during the day, or spotting southern women, Dravidians, and Andhras in dreams were all considered death omens.

The text even says physicians should discard patients with diseases like epilepsy, diabetes, or leprosy. So much for the “healing wisdom” of Ayurveda. Modern gurus like Baba Ramdev claim Ayurveda cures everything, but the actual texts show a bizarre obsession with omens, misogyny, and superstition.

From dreams of lotuses on your chest to flies buzzing after a bath, this isn’t science — it’s pseudoscience. Ayurveda might be ancient, but age doesn’t equal truth. Science demands evidence, not rhymes about death.

If you’ve searched for Ayurveda debunked, Caraka Samhita explained, Ayurveda myths, science of life vs signs of death, Baba Ramdev Ayurveda claims, or Pale Blue Thoughts Ayurveda video, this episode lays it all out.
